text: It was at Weatherend. <break time="0.8s" /> A great house full of pictures and treasures. <break time="0.8s" /> That John Marcher, after many years. <break time="0.8s" /> Found himself face to face again. <break time="0.8s" /> With May Bartram. <break time="0.8s" /> A woman whose face he half remembered. <break time="0.8s" /> He had the odd impression. <break time="0.8s" /> That their earlier meeting had mattered. <break time="0.8s" /> More than he could recall. <break time="0.8s" /> And that she, unlike himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Had kept every detail of it alive. <break time="0.8s" /> Through all the intervening years. <break time="0.8s" /> He began by recalling. <break time="0.8s" /> That they had met in Rome. <break time="0.8s" /> Some eight years before but she corrected him gently. <break time="0.8s" /> Saying that it had been at Naples. <break time="0.8s" /> And nearer ten years than eight. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, with a quiet smile. <break time="0.8s" /> She reminded him. <break time="0.8s" /> Of something he had entirely forgotten. <break time="0.8s" /> Namely that during one of those Italian afternoons. <break time="0.8s" /> He had confided to her. <break time="0.8s" /> A strange and deeply private secret. <break time="0.8s" /> He had told her. <break time="0.8s" /> That he had always felt. <break time="0.8s" /> Deep within himself. <break time="0.8s" /> That something rare and strange. <break time="0.8s" /> Possibly prodigious and terrible. <break time="0.8s" /> Was waiting for him. <break time="0.8s" /> And would sooner or later happen. <break time="0.8s" /> Hearing that she had kept his secret. <break time="0.8s" /> For ten years. <break time="0.8s" /> Without sharing it with anyone. <break time="0.8s" /> Marcher felt. <break time="0.8s" /> For the first time in his life. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was no longer. <break time="0.8s" /> Entirely alone with it. <break time="0.8s" /> Has it ever happened, she asked. <break time="0.8s" /> And when he answered. <break time="0.8s" /> That it had not she listened without a trace of mockery. <break time="0.8s" /> And soon they agreed. <break time="0.8s" /> To watch for it together.
